1525.text: A body weighed $250 \mathrm{~N}$ on the surface assuming the earth to be a sphere of uniform mass density, how much would it weigh half way down to the centre of the earth?

2629.subject: Chemistry
2629.text: Which of the following vitamins cannot be stored in the body?
2629.sol:
Vitamins are classified into two groups depending upon their solubility in water or fat.

Fat soluble vitamins: Vitamins which are soluble in fat and oils but insoluble in water are kept in this group. These are vitamins $A, D, E$ and $K$. They are stored in liver and adipose (fat storing) tissues.

Water soluble vitamins: $B$ group vitamins and vitamin $C$ are soluble in water. Water soluble vitamins must be supplied regularly in diet because they are readily excreted in urine and cannot be stored (except vitamin ${B}_{12}$) in our body.

We know that the average kinetic energy depends on the temperature and number of moles.&

$\left(K . E .\right)A = \dfrac{3{n}_{A}{RT}_{A } }{2}$

$\left(K . E .\right)B = \dfrac{3{n}_{B}{RT}_{B}}{2}$
Assume common mass$= m$
${n}_{A} = m / 2{n}_{B} = m / 44$

$\dfrac{\left(K . E .\right)A}{\left(K . E .\right)B} = \dfrac{{n}_{A}{T}_{A}}{{n}_{B}{T}_{B}} = \dfrac{m / 2 \times 300}{m / 44 \times 600} = 11: 1$

6349.subject: Mathematics
6349.text: The function $f(x)=x^3+a x^2+b x+c, a^2 \leq 3 b$ has
options: one maximum and one minimum value
one maximum and one minimum value
6349.sol:
Given, $f(x)=x^3+a x^2+b x+c, a^2 \leq 3 b$.
On differentiating w.r.t. $x$, we get
$\begin{aligned} & f^{\prime}(x)=3 x^2+2 a x+b \\ & \text{ Put } \quad f^{\prime}(x)=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad 3 x^2+2 a x+b=0 \\ & \end{aligned}\begin{aligned}
\Rightarrow \quad x & =\frac{-2 a \pm \sqrt{4 a^2-12 b}}{2 \times 3} \\
& =\frac{-2 a \pm 2 \sqrt{a^2-3 b}}{3}
\end{aligned}$
Since, $\quad a^2 \leq 3 b$, $\therefore \quad x$ has an imaginary value. Hence, no extreme value of $x$ exist.

8492.text: If $u=\sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{x^2+y^2}{x+y}\right)$ then $x \frac{\partial u}{\partial x}+y \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}$ equal to :

18038.text: If $n$ is a positive integer, then $2.4^{2 n+1}+3^{3 n+1}$ is divisible by:
18038.sol:
Let $P(n)=2 \cdot 4^{2 n+1}+3^{3 n+1}$
Then $P(1)=2.4^3+3^4=209$, which is divisible by 11 but not divisible by 2,7 or 27.
Further, let $P(k)=2.4^{2 k+1}+3^{3 k+1}$ is divisible by 11 , that is,
$2.4^{2 k+1}+3^{3 k+1}=11 q$ for some integer q. Now
$\begin{aligned} \\ \mathrm{P}(\mathrm{k}+1) & =2 \cdot 4^{2 \mathrm{k}+3}+3^{3 \mathrm{k}+4} \\ \\ & =2 \cdot 4^{2 \mathrm{k}+1} \cdot 4^2+3^{3 \mathrm{k}+1} \cdot 3^3 \\ \\ & =16 \cdot 2 \cdot 4^{2 \mathrm{k}+1}+27 \cdot 3^{3 \mathrm{k}+1} \\ \\ & =16 \cdot 2 \cdot 4^{2 \mathrm{k}+1}+(16+11) \cdot 3^{3 \mathrm{k}+1} \\ \\ & =16\left[2 \cdot 4^{2 \mathrm{k}+1}+3^{3 \mathrm{k}+1}\right]+11 \cdot 3^{3 \mathrm{k}+1} \\ \\ & =16 \cdot 11 \mathrm{q}+11 \cdot 3^{3 \mathrm{k}+1} \\ \\ & =11\left(16 \mathrm{q}+3^{3 \mathrm{k}+1}\right)=11 \mathrm{ m} \\ \end{aligned}$
where $m=16 q+3^{3 k+1}$ is another integer.
$\therefore \mathrm{P}(\mathrm{k}+1)$ is divisible by 11.

19560.subject: Chemistry
19560.text:
Identify the final product formed when Toluene undergoes a series of reactions with reagents given in the order:
(i) $\mathrm{Cl}_2$ / Sunlight
(ii) $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} / 373 \mathrm{ K}$
(iii) Acetophenone / $\mathrm{OH^-}$ at $293 \mathrm{ K}$
19560.sol:
Toluene reacts with $\mathrm{Cl}_2$ in the presence of sunlight to undergo free radical chlorination at the side chain, yielding benzal chloride, $\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{CHCl}_2$.

Hydrolysis of benzal chloride with $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$ at $373 \mathrm{ K}$ replaces the two chlorine atoms with an oxygen atom to form benzaldehyde, $\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{CHO}$.

The reaction of benzaldehyde with acetophenone ($\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{COCH}_3$) in the presence of a base ($\mathrm{OH}^{-}$) is a Claisen-Schmidt condensation reaction. This reaction involves the nucleophilic attack of the enolate ion of acetophenone on the carbonyl carbon of benzaldehyde, followed by dehydration to form an $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated ketone.

The product formed is $\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CHCOC}_6\mathrm{H}_5$, which is 1,3-diphenylprop-2-en-1-one, commonly known as benzalacetophenone or chalcone.

Answer: 1, 3-Diphenylprop-2-en-1-one

20641.subject: Chemistry
20641.text: For a 1.0 molal solution containing the non-volatile solute Urea, the elevation in boiling point is 2.0 K while the depression in freezing point in a 3.0 molal solution having the same solvent is $4.0 K$. If the ratio $\dfrac{K_b}{K_f}=\dfrac{1}{X}$, what is the value of $X$ ?
20641.sol:
The elevation in boiling point is given by $\Delta T_b = K_b \times m_1$, where $m_1 = 1.0$ molal and $\Delta T_b = 2.0$ K. Thus, $2.0 = K_b \times 1.0$, which implies $K_b = 2.0$ K kg mol^{-1}$.

The depression in freezing point is given by $\Delta T_f = K_f \times m_2$, where $m_2 = 3.0$ molal and $\Delta T_f = 4.0$ K. Thus, 4.0 = K_f \times 3.0$, which implies $K_f = \dfrac{4.0}{3.0} = \dfrac{4}{3}$ K kg mol^{-1}$.

The ratio \dfrac{K_b}{K_f}$ is calculated as $\dfrac{2.0}{4/3} = 2.0 \times \dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{6}{4} = \dfrac{3}{2}$.

Given $\dfrac{K_b}{K_f} = \dfrac{1}{X}$, we have $\dfrac{3}{2} = \dfrac{1}{X}$, which implies $X = \dfrac{2}{3}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{2}{3}$

20962.sol:
The function is given by $f(x) = a + (x - 4)^{\dfrac{4}{9}}$.

The term $(x - 4)^{\dfrac{4}{9}}$ can be written as $\sqrt[$9]{(x - 4)^4}$. Since the exponent \dfrac{4}{9}$ has an even numerator, the expression $(x - 4)^4$ is always non-negative for all real $x$.

The minimum value of $(x - 4)^4$ is $0$, which occurs at $x = 4$.

Consequently, the minimum value of $(x - 4)^{\dfrac{4}{9}}$ is $0^{\dfrac{4}{9}} = 0$.

Therefore, the minimum value of $f(x) = a + (x - 4)^{\dfrac{4}{9}}$ is $a + 0 = a$.

Answer: a

20968.text: The approximate value of $f(5.001)$, where $f(x)=x^{3}-7 x^{2}+15$ is
20968.sol:
The function is given by $f(x) = x^{3} - 7x^{2} + 15$.

Using the linear approximation formula $f(x + \Delta x) \approx f(x) + f'(x) \Delta x$, we set $x = 5$ and $\Delta x = 0.001$.

First, calculate $f(5) = (5)^{3} - 7(5)^{2} + 15 = 125 - 7(25) + 15 = 125 - 175 + 15 = -35$.

Next, find the derivative $f'(x) = 3x^{2} - 14x$.

Evaluate the derivative at $x = 5$: $f'(5) = 3(5)^{2} - 14(5) = 3(25) - 70 = 75 - 70 = 5$.

Now, calculate the approximate value $f(5.001) \approx f(5) + f'(5) \Delta x = -35 + 5(0.001) = -35 + 0.005 = -34.995$.

Answer: $-34.995$

21488.subject: Mathematics
21488.text: Equation of a hyperbola having foci at $(0, \pm \sqrt{10})$ and passing through the point $(2,3)$ is
21488.sol:
The foci of the hyperbola are at $(0, \pm \sqrt{10})$, which implies the hyperbola is vertical with its center at $(0,0)$. The equation is of the form $\dfrac{y^2}{a^2} - \dfrac{x^2}{b^2} = 1$.

The distance of the foci from the center is $ae = \sqrt{10}$, so $a^2 e^2 = 10$. For a hyperbola, $b^2 = a^2(e^2 - 1) = a^2 e^2 - a^2$. Substituting the known values, $b^2 = 10 - a^2$.

The hyperbola passes through $(2,3)$. Substituting these coordinates into the equation: $\dfrac{3^2}{a^2} - \dfrac{2^2}{b^2} = 1$, which simplifies to $\dfrac{9}{a^2} - \dfrac{4}{10 - a^2} = 1$.

Let $u = a^2$. Then $\dfrac{9}{u} - \dfrac{4}{10 - u} = 1$. Multiplying by $u(10 - u)$, we get $9(10 - u) - 4u = u(10 - u)$.

$90 - 9u - 4u = 10u - u^2 \Rightarrow u^2 - 23u + 90 = 0$.

Factoring the quadratic equation: $(u - 18)(u - 5) = 0$. Thus $a^2 = 5$ or $a^2 = 18$.

If $a^2 = 5$, then $b^2 = 10 - 5 = 5$. The equation is $\dfrac{y^2}{5} - \dfrac{x^2}{5} = 1$, which is $y^2 - x^2 = 5$.

If $a^2 = 18$, then $b^2 = 10 - 18 = -8$, which is impossible for a hyperbola. Therefore, the equation is $y^2 - x^2 = 5$.

Answer: $y^2-x^2=5$

25199.subject: Mathematics
25199.text:
Let $P$ be the point on the parabola $y = x^2$ such that the slope of the tangent to the parabola at the point $P$ is $4$. Let $Q$ be the point in the first quadrant lying on the circle $x^2 + y^2 = 2$ such that the slope of the tangent to the circle at the point $Q$ is $-1$. Let $R$ be the point in the first quadrant lying on the ellipse $x^2 + 4y^2 = 8$ such that the slope of the tangent to the ellipse at the point $R$ is $-\dfrac{1}{2}$.

Then the radius of the circle passing through the points $P, Q$ and $R$ is
25199.sol:
For the point $P$ on the parabola $y = x^2$, the slope of the tangent is $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2x$.
Given $2x = 4 \Rightarrow x = 2$.
Substituting $x = 2$ in $y = x^2$, we get $y = 4$.
Thus, the coordinates of $P$ are $(2, 4)$.

For the point $Q$ on the circle $x^2 + y^2 = 2$, differentiating with respect to $x$ gives $2x + 2y \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0 \Rightarrow \dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{x}{y}$.
Given $-\dfrac{x}{y} = -1 \Rightarrow x = y$.
Since $Q$ lies in the first quadrant, substituting $x = y$ in $x^2 + y^2 = 2$ gives $2x^2 = 2 \Rightarrow x = 1, y = 1$.
Thus, the coordinates of $Q$ are $(1, 1)$.

For the point $R$ on the ellipse $x^2 + 4y^2 = 8$, differentiating with respect to $x$ gives $2x + 8y \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0 \Rightarrow \dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{x}{4y}$.
Given $-\dfrac{x}{4y} = -\dfrac{1}{2} \Rightarrow x = 2y$.
Since $R$ lies in the first quadrant, substituting $x = 2y$ in $x^2 + 4y^2 = 8$ gives $4y^2 + 4y^2 = 8 \Rightarrow 8y^2 = 8 \Rightarrow y = 1, x = 2$.
Thus, the coordinates of $R$ are $(2, 1)$.

The points are $P(2, 4)$, $Q(1, 1)$, and $R(2, 1)$.
The line segment $PR$ lies on the vertical line $x = 2$, and the line segment $QR$ lies on the horizontal line $y = 1$.
Since $PR$ is perpendicular to $QR$, the angle $\angle PRQ = 90^{\circ}$.
Therefore, the triangle $PQR$ is a right-angled triangle with the hypotenuse $PQ$.
The circumcircle of $\triangle PQR$ has $PQ$ as its diameter.
The length of the diameter is $PQ = \sqrt{(2 - 1)^2 + (4 - 1)^2} = \sqrt{1^2 + 3^2} = \sqrt{10}$.
The radius of the circle is $\dfrac{PQ}{2} = \dfrac{\sqrt{10}}{2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{5}{2}}$.

Answer: $\sqrt{\dfrac{5}{2}}$

27703.subject: Chemistry
27703.text:
$SF_4$ is isostructural with:
A. $BrF_4^{\ominus}$
B. $CH_4$
C. $IF_4^{\oplus}$
D. $XeF_4$
E. $XeO_2 F_2$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
27703.sol:
In $SF_4$, the central sulphur atom has $6$ valence electrons. It forms $4$ sigma bonds with fluorine atoms and has $1$ lone pair. The steric number is $5$, corresponding to $sp^3d$ hybridization, and the shape is see-saw.

In $BrF_4^{\ominus}$, the central bromine atom has $8$ valence electrons ($7 + 1$). It forms $4$ sigma bonds and has $2$ lone pairs. The steric number is $6$, corresponding to $sp^3d^2$ hybridization, and the shape is square planar.

In $CH_4$, the central carbon atom has $4$ valence electrons. It forms $4$ sigma bonds and has $0$ lone pairs. The steric number is $4$, corresponding to $sp^3$ hybridization, and the shape is tetrahedral.

In $IF_4^{\oplus}$, the central iodine atom has $6$ valence electrons ($7 - 1$). It forms $4$ sigma bonds and has $1$ lone pair. The steric number is $5$, corresponding to $sp^3d$ hybridization, and the shape is see-saw.

In $XeF_4$, the central xenon atom has $8$ valence electrons. It forms $4$ sigma bonds and has $2$ lone pairs. The steric number is $6$, corresponding to $sp^3d^2$ hybridization, and the shape is square planar.

In $XeO_2F_2$, the central xenon atom has $8$ valence electrons. It forms $4$ sigma bonds ($2$ with oxygen, $2$ with fluorine), $2$ pi bonds, and has $1$ lone pair. The steric number is $5$, corresponding to $sp^3d$ hybridization, and the shape is see-saw.

Therefore, $IF_4^{\oplus}$ and $XeO_2F_2$ are isostructural with $SF_4$.

Answer: C and E Only

29296.subject: Chemistry
29296.text:
Consider the following reduction processes :
$\mathrm{Al}^{3+}+3 \mathrm{e}^{-} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Al}(\mathrm{s}), \mathrm{E}^{0}=-1.66 \mathrm{~V}$
$\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}+\mathrm{e}^{-} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Fe}^{2+}, \mathrm{E}^{0}=+0.77 \mathrm{~V}$
$\mathrm{Co}^{3+}+\mathrm{e}^{-} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Co}^{2+}, \mathrm{E}^{0}=+1.81 \mathrm{~V}$
$\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}+3 \mathrm{e}^{-} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{s}), \mathrm{E}^{\circ}=-0.74 \mathrm{~V}$
The tendency to act as reducing agent decreases in the order :
29296.sol:
Reducing agent strength is determined by oxidation potential (opposite sign of reduction potential). Stronger reducing agents have more negative oxidation potentials (easier to oxidize).
Oxidation potentials:
Al(s) → Al³⁺ has E° = +1.66 V (strongest reducing agent);
Cr(s) → Cr³⁺ has E° = +0.74 V;
Fe²⁺ → Fe³⁺ has E° = -0.77 V;
Co²⁺ → Co³⁺ has E° = -1.81 V (weakest reducing agent).
Order of decreasing reducing agent tendency: Al > Cr > Fe²⁺ > Co²⁺.

31267.subject: Chemistry
31267.text: By usual analysis, 1.00 g of compound $(\mathrm{X})$ gave 1.79 g of magnesium pyrophosphate. The percentage of phosphorus in compound $(X)$ is : (nearest integer) (Given, molar mass in $\mathrm{g} \mathrm{mol}^{-1}: \mathrm{O}=16, \mathrm{Mg}=24, \mathrm{P}=31$)
31267.sol:
Given: 1.00 g of compound (X) produces 1.79 g of Mg₂P₂O₇.
Molar mass of Mg₂P₂O₇ = 2(24) + 2(31) + 7(16) = 222 g/mol.
Moles of Mg₂P₂O₇ = 1.79 / 222 = 0.00806 mol.
Since each mole of Mg₂P₂O₇ contains 2 moles of P, moles of P = 2 × 0.00806 = 0.01612 mol.
Mass of P = 0.01612 × 31 = 0.4997 g ≈ 0.50 g.
Percentage of phosphorus = (0.50 / 1.00) × 100 = 50%.

37199.text: Three numbers are in an increasing geometric progression with common ratio $r .$ If the middle number is doubled, then the new numbers are in an arithmetic progression with common difference $d .$ If the fourth term of GP is $3{r}^{2},$ then ${r}^{2} - d$ is equal to :
37199.sol:
Three numbers are in an increasing geometric progression with common ratio $r .$

Let first term is $a$

$⇒ \dfrac{a}{r}, a, ar \in G . P$

Given that if middle term is doubled

$⇒ \dfrac{a}{r}, 2a, ar \in A . P$

If $a, b, c \in A . P ⇒ 2b = a + c$
$4a = ar + \dfrac{a}{r}$

$4 = r + \dfrac{1}{r}$

${r}^{2} + 1 = 4r$

${r}^{2} - 4r + 1 = 0$

If$a{x}^{2} + bx + c = 0 ⇒ x = \dfrac{- b \pm \sqrt{{b}^{2} - 4ac}}{2ac}$

$⇒ r = \dfrac{4 \pm \sqrt{12}}{2} = 2 + \sqrt{3}, 2 - \sqrt{3}$

But it is an increasing $G . P$

$∴ r = 2 + \sqrt{3}$

Given that Fourth term of $G . P ⇒ {t}_{4} = a{r}^{2} = 3{r}^{2}$

$⇒ a = 3 .$

Common difference of an $A . P = d = {t}_{2} - {t}_{1}$

$d = 2a - \dfrac{a}{r} = a\left(2 - \dfrac{1}{r}\right) = 3\left(2 - \dfrac{1}{2 + \sqrt{3}}\right)$

$= 3 ( 2 - 2 + \sqrt{3} ) = 3\sqrt{3}$
Hence ${r}^{2} - d = ( 2 + \sqrt{3}{)}^{2} - ( 3\sqrt{3} )$

$= 4 + 3 + 4\sqrt{3} - 3\sqrt{3}$

$= 7 + \sqrt{3}$

37728.text: Let the equations of two adjacent sides of a parallelogram $ABCD$ be $2x - 3y = - 23$ and $5x + 4y = 23$. If the equation of its one diagonal $AC$ is $3x + 7y = 23$  and the distance of $A$ from the other diagonal is $d$, then $50{d}^{2}$ is equal to ______________
37728.sol:
Given,

The equations of two adjacent sides of a parallelogram $ABCD$ be $2x - 3y = - 23 and 5x + 4y = 23$,

So, $AB ≡ 2x - 3y = - 23 and BC ≡ 5x + 4y = 23$

Also given, $AC ≡ 3x + 7y = 23$

Solving the above lines we get, A ( – 4, 5 ) , B ( – 1, 7 ) , C ( 3, 2 )$

We know that,

Diagonal of parallelogram have same midpoint,

So $AC and BD$ have same mid-point and let point $D$ be \left(x, y\right),

So midpoint formula we get,

\dfrac{x - 1}{2} = \dfrac{- 4 + 3}{2}$ ⇒ x = 0 and $\dfrac{y + 7}{2} = \dfrac{2 + 5}{2} ⇒ y = 0$

Hence, point $D$ is $( 0, 0 )$

Now Equation of $BD$ will be $7x + y = 0$

Now finding the distance of A $\left(- 4, 5\right)$ from $7x + y = 0$ we get,

$d = \left|\dfrac{7 ( - 4 ) + 5}{\sqrt{{7}^{2} + {1}^{2}}}\right| = \dfrac{23}{\sqrt{50}}$

Hence, $50{d}^{2} = {23}^{2} = 529$

37822.text: If a line $L$ is perpendicular to the line $5x - y = 1,$ and the area of the triangle formed by the line $L$ and the coordinate axes is $5$ sq units, then the distance of the line $L$ from the line $x + 5y = 0$ is
37822.sol:
The equation of a line perpendicular to the line $ax + by + c = 0$ is $bx - ay + k = 0, k \in R .$

Given, line $L$ is perpendicular to $5x - y = 1,$ hence the equation of $L$ is $x +5 y + k =0$

For finding $x$-Intercept, put $y = 0$

$⇒ x + k = 0, ⇒ x = - k$

$∴$ $x$-intercept$= - k$

Similarly, for finding $y$- Intercept, put $x = 0$

$⇒ 5y + k = 0, ⇒ y = - \dfrac{k}{5}$

$∴$ $y$-intercept$= - \dfrac{k}{5}$

Given, the area formed by the line $L$ with the coordinate axes is $5$ sq units.

Hence, the area of $\text{\Delta =}\dfrac{1}{2} \times \left(- k\right)\left(- \dfrac{k}{5}\right) = 5$

$⇒ {k}^{2} = 50$

$⇒ k = \pm \text{5}\sqrt{2}$

Hence, the equation of the line is $L: x ⁡+5 y ⁡ \pm 5 \sqrt{2} = 0$

Now, we know that the distance between the parallel lines $ax + by + c = 0$ and $ax + by + {c}_{1} = 0$ is $\dfrac{\left|c - {c}_{1}\right|}{\sqrt{{a}^{2} + {b}^{2}}}$

Thus, the distance between the lines $x +5 y =0$ and $x +5 y\text{⁡ \pm 5}\sqrt{2} = 0$ is

$d = \left|\dfrac{\pm 5\sqrt{2} - 0}{\sqrt{{1}^{2} + {5}^{2}}}\right|$

$⇒ d = \dfrac{5\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{26}}$

$⇒ d = \dfrac{5\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{13 \times 2}} = \dfrac{5}{\sqrt{13}}$ units.

38296.text: The number of elements in the set $\left\{x \in\left[0,180^{\circ}\right]: $\tan$\left(x+100^{\circ}\right)=\tan \left(x+50^{\circ}\right)$\tan x\tan$\left(x-50^{\circ}\right)\right\}$ is $\_\_\_\_$.
38296.sol:
$\frac{\tan(x+100°)}{\tan x} = \tan(x+50°)\tan(x-50°)$
$\frac{\sin(x+100°)\cos x}{\cos(x+100°)\sin x} = \frac{\sin(x+50°)\sin(x-50°)}{\cos(x+50°)\cos(x-50°)}$
Applying Componendo & Dividendo:
$\frac{\sin(2x+100°)}{\sin 100°} = \frac{\cos 100°}{-\cos 2x}$
$2\sin(2x+100°)\cos 2x + \sin 200° = 0$
$\sin(4x+100°) + \sin 100° + \sin 200° = 0$
$\sin(4x+100°) = -2\sin 150° \cos 50°$
$\sin(4x+100°) = -\cos 50° = \sin(-40°)$
$\therefore 4x + 100° = n\pi + (-1)^n(-40°)$
$x = \frac{n\pi + (-1)^{n+1}(40°) - 100°}{4}$
$\therefore x = 30°, 55°, 120°, 145°$ in $(0, \pi)$
$\therefore$ Number of solutions $= 4$

Then for resistance ${R}_{3}$, the potential difference will be

${V}_{3} = {i}_{1}{R}_{3} = 0 . 01 \times 100 = 1V$

So, for given branch of resistance potential difference is

From figure for resistance ${R}_{1}, {R}_{3}$ and ${R}_{4}$ a total applied potential difference is $18V$ then,

${V}_{1} + {V}_{3} + {V}_{4} = 18 ∴ {V}_{1} = 18 - \left({V}_{3} + {V}_{4}\right) = 18 - 6 = 12V$

So, the total current drawn from the source is

$∴$ Current through ${R}_{2}$

${i}_{2} = 0 \cdot 03 - 0 \cdot 01 = 0 \cdot 02A$
and potential difference for ${R}_{2}$ is

${V}_{2} = {V}_{3} + {V}_{4} = 6V$ ( ${R}_{2}$ is in parallel arrangement with the resistances ${R}_{3}$ and ${R}_{4}$)

Now the value of resistance ${R}_{2}$ is :
${V}_{2} = {i}_{2}{R}_{2} ⇒ {R}_{2} = \dfrac{{V}_{2}}{{i}_{2}} = \dfrac{6}{0 \cdot 02} = 300Ω$

47875.subject: Chemistry
47875.text: Which of the following is the strongest base?
47875.sol:
We know, an anion is strongest base, if its conjugate acid is weakest.
Here, $\mathrm{CH}_{3} \mathrm{COO}^{-}$ will have conjugate acid $\mathrm{CH}_{3} \mathrm{COOH}$.
$\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$ will have conjugate acid HCl.
$\mathrm{OH}^{-}$ will have conjugate acid HOH. $\mathrm{CH}_{3} \mathrm{O}^{-}$ will have conjugate acid $\mathrm{CH}_{3} \mathrm{OH}$.
Since, out of above four, $\mathrm{CH}_{3} \mathrm{OH}$ will be the weakest acid and hence, $\mathrm{CH}_{3} \mathrm{O}^{-}$ will be strongest base.

53717.text:
Let $f(x)$ be differentiable on the interval $(0, \infty)$ such that $f(1)=1$ and
$\lim _{t \rightarrow x} \frac{t^2 f(x)-x^2 f(t)}{t-x}=1$ for each $x>0$
Then, $f(x)$ is equal to
53717.sol:
Given, $\lim _{t \rightarrow x} \frac{t^2 f(x)-x^2 f(t)}{t-x}=1$
Using L' Hospital's rule, we get
$\lim _{t \rightarrow x} \frac{t^2 f^{\prime}(x)-2 x f(t)}{-1}=1\Rightarrow \quad x^2 f^{\prime}(x)-2 x f(x)+1=0\Rightarrow \quad \frac{x^2 f^{\prime}(x)-2 x f(x)}{\left(x^2\right)^2}+\frac{1}{x^4}=0\Rightarrow \quad \frac{d}{d x}\left(\frac{f(x)}{x^2}\right)=-\frac{1}{x^4}$
On integrating both sides, we get
$\frac{f(x)}{x^2}=+\frac{1}{3 x^3}+c \Rightarrow f(x)=\frac{1}{3 x}+c x^2$
Also, $\quad f(1)=1 \Rightarrow 1=\frac{1}{3 \times 1}+c(1)^2\Rightarrow \quad 1=\frac{1}{3}+c \Rightarrow \frac{2}{3}=c\therefore \quad f(x)=\frac{1}{3 x}+\frac{2 x^2}{3}$

55248.text: Which from following amines when heated with ethanolic KOH and chloroform does NOT produce foul smell ?
55248.sol:
The reaction of an amine with chloroform and ethanolic KOH to produce a foul-smelling compound is known as the carbylamine test or isocyanide test.

This test is given only by primary aliphatic and primary aromatic amines. Secondary and tertiary amines do not respond to this test.

Benzenamine is a primary aromatic amine.

Propan-2-amine is a primary aliphatic amine.

Phenylmethanamine is a primary aliphatic amine.

N,N-Dimethyl aniline is a tertiary amine, so it does not give the carbylamine test and will not produce a foul smell.

Answer: N , N - Dimethyl aniline

59138.subject: Chemistry
59138.text: Calculate vapour pressure of volatile liquid $A$ at given temperature if mole fraction and vapour pressure of volatile liquid B are 0.4 and 900 mm Hg respectively [ $\mathrm{P}_{\text{total }}=600 \mathrm{~mm} \mathrm{Hg}$ ]
59138.sol:
Vapor pressure of volatile liquid A

The mole fraction of component A is determined from the binary composition: $X_A = 1 - X_B = 1 - 0.4 = 0.6$.

Applying Raoult's law for the total vapor pressure, $P_{\text{total}} = X_A P_A^0 + X_B P_B^0$.

Substituting known values: $600 = 0.6 P_A^0 + (0.4)(900)$.

Solving for $P_A^0$: $600 - 360 = 0.6 P_A^0$
$240 = 0.6 P_A^0$
$P_A^0 = \frac{240}{0.6} = 400$

The vapor pressure of volatile liquid A is $\boxed{400 \text{ mm Hg}}$.

59622.text: Calculate the shortest wavelength in hydrogen spectrum emission of Lymen series ($R_H = 109677\,\text{cm}^{-1}$)
59622.sol:
For the Lyman series, the transition is from $n_2 to n_1 = 1$.

The shortest wavelength corresponds to the maximum energy transition, which occurs when $n_2 = \infty$.

Using the Rydberg formula:

$\dfrac{1}{\lambda} = R_H \left( \dfrac{1}{n_1^2} - \dfrac{1}{n_2^2} \right)

Substituting $ n_1 = 1 and n_2 = $\infty:

\dfrac{1}{\lambda} =$ R_H $\left( \dfrac{1}{1^2} - \dfrac{1}{\infty^2} \right) =$ R_H$

$\lambda = $\dfrac{1}{R_H}

Given $ R_H = 109677 $\text{ cm}^{-1}:

$\lambda = $\dfrac{1}{109677} \text{ cm} \approx9.117 \times10^{-6} \text{ cm}

Answer: 9.117 \times10^{-6}$ cm

59630.subject: Chemistry
59630.text: What is the observed electronic configuration of Cu ?
59630.sol:
The atomic number of copper (Cu) is $29$.

According to the Aufbau principle, the expected electronic configuration is $[\text{Ar}]\ 3d^9\ 4s^2$.

However, a completely filled $d$-subshell ($3d^{10}$) provides extra stability due to symmetrical electron distribution and higher exchange energy.

Therefore, one electron from the $4s$ orbital is transferred to the $3d$ orbital, resulting in the observed electronic configuration of $[\text{Ar}]\ 3d^{10}\ 4s^1$.

Answer: $[\text{Ar}]\ 3d^{10}\ 4s^1$

62968.subject: Mathematics
62968.text:
p : If 7 is an odd number then 7 is divisible by 2
q : If 7 is prime number then 7 is an odd number
If $V_1 and V_2$ are respective truth values of contrapositive of $p and q$ then $\left(V_1, V_2\right) \equiv$
62968.sol:
The statement $p$ asserts that "If 7 is an odd number, then 7 is divisible by 2," represented as $A ightarrow B$, where $A$ is true and $B$ is false. The truth value $T ightarrow F$ evaluates to false.

The contrapositive of $A ightarrow B$ is $ eg B ightarrow eg A$, which always shares the same truth value as the original statement. For $p$, where $ eg B$ is true and $ eg A$ is false, $T ightarrow F$ also gives false. Therefore, $V_1 = F$.

The statement $q$ is "If 7 is a prime number, then 7 is an odd number," or $C ightarrow D$, with both $C$ and $D$ true. The value $T ightarrow T$ is true. Its contrapositive, $ eg D ightarrow eg C$, with both false, yields $F ightarrow F$, which is true. Thus, $V_2 = T$.

Together, $(V_1, V_2) = (F, T)$, corresponding to option C.

63556.subject: Mathematics
63556.text: A random variable $X \sim B(n, p)$ follows a binomial distribution with $n = 6$. If $9P(X = 4) = P(X = 2)$, then the probability of success $p$ is..
63556.sol:
Given $X \sim B(n, p)$ with $n = 6$.

The probability mass function is $P(X = k) = ^{n}C_{k} p^k (1-p)^{n-k}$.

Substituting $k = 4$ and $k = 2$ in the given condition $9P(X = 4) = P(X = 2)$:

$9 \times ^{6}C_{4} p^4 (1-p)^2 = ^{6}C_{2} p^2 (1-p)^4$

Since ^{6}C_{4} = ^{6}C_{2} = 15$, dividing both sides by 15 p^2 (1-p)^2$ gives:

$9p^2 = (1-p)^2$

Taking the square root on both sides, since $p > 0$ and $1-p > 0$:

$3p = 1 - p$

$4p = 1$

$p = 0.25$

Answer: $0.25$

=$\frac{1}{5}+\frac{4}{15}+\frac{2}{15}$\\

\end{array}$

63948.subject: Mathematics
63948.text: In $\triangle ABC$, with usual notations, if $\Delta$ denotes the area of triangle $ABC$ then the value of $2s(b+c-a)\tan \left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right) is equal to $\ldots
63948.sol:
We know that the semi-perimeter of a triangle is given by $s = \dfrac{a+b+c}{2}$, which implies $2s = a+b+c$.

The term $b+c-a$ can be rewritten as:

$b+c-a = (a+b+c) - 2a = 2s - 2a = 2(s-a)$

Substituting this into the given expression, we get:

$2s(b+c-a)\tan \left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right) =2s(2(s-a))\tan\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right) =4s(s-a)\tan\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)

Using the half-angle formula for tangents in a triangle:

\tan\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right) = \sqrt{\dfrac{(s-b)(s-c)}{s(s-a)}}

Multiplying the numerator and the denominator inside the square root by $ s(s-a)$ gives:

\tan\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right) = \dfrac{\sqrt{s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)}}{s(s-a)}

By Heron's formula, the area of the triangle is \Delta = \sqrt{s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)}. Therefore:

\tan\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right) = \dfrac{\Delta}{s(s-a)}

Substituting this back into the modified expression:

4s(s-a)\tan\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right) =4s(s-a) \times \dfrac{\Delta}{s(s-a)} =4\Delta$

Answer: $4\Delta$

63993.subject: Mathematics
63993.text: In a triangle ABC , the sides $a, \mathrm{ b}, \mathrm{c}$ are such that they are the roots of the equation $x^3-11 x^2+38 x-40=0$ Then $\frac{\cos \mathrm{A}}{a}+\frac{\cos \mathrm{B}}{\mathrm{b}}+\frac{\cos \mathrm{C}}{\mathrm{c}}=$
63993.sol:
The sides of the triangle are the roots of the equation $x^3 - 11x^2 + 38x - 40 = 0$. Testing integer divisors of 40 reveals that $x = 2$ is a root. Dividing the cubic polynomial by $(x - 2)$ yields $x^2 - 9x + 20$, which factors as $(x - 4)(x - 5)$. The sides are therefore $2$, $4$, and $5$ in some order.

Using the Law of Cosines, $\cos A = \frac{b^2 + c^2 - a^2}{2bc}$, with similar expressions for $\cos B$ and $\cos C$. Substituting into $\frac{\cos A}{a} + \frac{\cos B}{b} + \frac{\cos C}{c}$ gives $\frac{b^2 + c^2 - a^2}{2abc} + \frac{a^2 + c^2 - b^2}{2abc} + \frac{a^2 + b^2 - c^2}{2abc}$.

The sum simplifies to $\frac{a^2 + b^2 + c^2}{2abc}$, as the numerator reduces to $a^2 + b^2 + c^2$ after cancellation.

With side lengths $2$, $4$, and $5$, $a^2 + b^2 + c^2 = 4 + 16 + 25 = 45$ and $abc = 40$. The expression evaluates to $\frac{45}{80} = \frac{9}{16}$.

Final answer: $\frac{9}{16}$

64075.text: If triangle $A B C$ is a right angled at $A$ and $\tan \frac{B}{2}, \tan \frac{C}{2}$ are roots of the equation $a x^2+b x+c=0, a \neq 0$, then
64075.sol:
The quadratic equation $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$ has roots $\tan\frac{B}{2}$ and $\tan\frac{C}{2}$,
giving the root relationships:

$\tan\frac{B}{2} + \tan\frac{C}{2} = -\frac{b}{a}$
$\tan\frac{B}{2} \cdot \tan\frac{C}{2} = \frac{c}{a}$

For a right triangle with angle $A = 90^{}^{\circ}$, the angle sum $B + C = 90^{}^{\circ}$ implies $\frac{B+C}{2} = 45^{}^{\circ}$.
Applying the tangent sum identity:

$\frac{\tan\frac{B}{2} + \tan\frac{C}{2}}{1 - \tan\frac{B}{2} \cdot \tan\frac{C}{2}} = \tan 45^{}^{\circ} = 1$

Substituting the root relationships:

$\frac{-\frac{b}{a}}{1 - \frac{c}{a}} = 1$

Simplifying yields $-b = a - c$, or equivalently $a + b = c$.

This corresponds to option $\boxed{B}$.

64095.sol: Given the progression $a = \frac{1}{6} \sin \theta$, $b = \cos \theta$, $c = \tan \theta$ are in geometric progression, the condition holds: $b^2 = ac$. Substitute the expressions: $(\cos \theta)^2 = \left(\frac{1}{6} \sin \theta\right) (\tan \theta)$. Since $\tan \theta = \frac{\sin \theta}{\cos \theta}$, \(\cos^2 $\theta = \frac{1}{6} \sin \theta \cdot \frac{\sin \theta}{\cos \theta}.$\) Multiplying both sides by $\cos \theta$ ($\cos \theta \neq 0$): \(\cos^3 $\theta = \frac{1}{6} \sin^2 $\theta.$\) Using $\sin^2 \theta = 1 - \cos^2 \theta$: \(\cos^3 $\theta = \frac{1}{6}($1 - \cos^2 $\theta).$\) Multiply by 6 and rearrange: \(6 \cos^3 $\theta + \cos^2 $\theta -$1 = 0.\) Let $x = \cos \theta$: \(6x^3 + x² - 1 = 0.\) Check rational roots: $x = \frac{1}{2}$ satisfies the equation, so it is a root. Factor the cubic: $(2x - 1)(3x^2 + 2x + 1) = 0$. The quadratic factor $3x^2 + 2x + 1 = 0$ has discriminant $D = 4 - 12 = -8 \lt 0$, so no real roots. Thus, $\cos \theta = \frac{1}{2}$, and the general solution is $\theta = 2n\pi \pm \frac{\pi}{3}$, $n \in \mathbb{Z}$. The answer matches option A.

64951.text: The value of $\tan \frac{\pi}{3}+2 \tan \frac{2 \pi}{3}+4 \tan \frac{4 \pi}{3}+8 \tan \frac{8 \pi}{3}$ is equal to
64951.sol:
Evaluating the expression $\tan \frac{\pi}{3} + 2 \tan \frac{2\pi}{3} + 4 \tan \frac{4\pi}{3} + 8 \tan \frac{8\pi}{3}$ requires simplifying each term using trigonometric identities.

Using the known value $\tan \frac{\pi}{3} = \sqrt{3}$, the first term is $\sqrt{3}.

For the second term, \tan \frac{2\pi}{3} = \tan (\pi - \frac{\pi}{3}) = -\tan \frac{\pi}{3} = -\sqrt{3}$, so $2 \tan \frac{2\pi}{3} = -2\sqrt{3}$.

The third term simplifies as $\tan \frac{4\pi}{3} = \tan (\pi + \frac{\pi}{3}) = \tan \frac{\pi}{3} = \sqrt{3}$, giving $4 \tan \frac{4\pi}{3} = 4\sqrt{3}$.

Finally, $\tan \frac{8\pi}{3} = \tan (2\pi + \frac{2\pi}{3}) = \tan \frac{2\pi}{3} = -\sqrt{3}$, so $8 \tan \frac{8\pi}{3} = -8\sqrt{3}$.

Combining all terms: $\sqrt{3} -2\sqrt{3} +4\sqrt{3} -8\sqrt{3} = ($1 - 2 + 4 - $8)\sqrt{3} = -$-5\sqrt{3}.

The final result is \boxed{-5\sqrt{3}}$.

66211.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
66211.text: An object of mass ' $m$ ' moving with velocity ' $u$ ' collides with another stationary object of mass ' M ' and stops just after the collision. The coefficient of restitution is
66211.sol:
Coefficient of restitution determination:

Conservation of linear momentum applied to the collision yields $m u + M \cdot 0 = m \cdot 0 + M v_2$, which simplifies to $m u = M v_2$ and thus $v_2 = \frac{m u}{M}$.

The coefficient of restitution is defined as $e = \frac{v_2 - v_1}{u_1 - u_2}$. Substituting the known velocities $v_1 = 0$, $u_2 = 0$, and the expression for $v_2$ gives $e = \frac{\frac{m u}{M} - 0}{u - 0} = \frac{m}{M}$.

The result $e = \frac{m}{M}$ corresponds to option C.

66569.text: Sodium and copper have work functions $2 \times 3 \mathrm{ ev}$ and $4 \times 5 \mathrm{ ev}$ respectively. The ratio of threshold wavelength of sodium to that of copper is nearest to
66569.sol:
The work function $\phi$ for a metal with threshold wavelength $\lambda_0$ is given by $\phi = \frac{hc}{\lambda_0}$, where $h$ is Planck's constant and $c$ is the speed of light.

Rearranging gives $\lambda_0 = \frac{hc}{\phi}$ for any metal. The ratio of threshold wavelengths for sodium and copper is therefore:

$\frac{\lambda_{0,\text{Na}}}{\lambda_{0,\text{Cu}}} = \frac{\phi_{\text{Cu}}}{\phi_{\text{Na}}}$

Given work functions $\phi_{\text{Na}} = 2 \times 3 = 6\text{ eV}$ and $\phi_{\text{Cu}} = 4 \times 5 = 20\text{ eV}$, the ratio becomes:

$\frac{\lambda_{0,\text{Na}}}{\lambda_{0,\text{Cu}}} = \frac{20}{6} = \frac{10}{3} \approx 3.33$

Comparing with the options:
A) $0.25$
B) $4$
C) $0.5$
D) $2$

The value $3.33$ is nearest to option B.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{B}}$

67673.text: A circular coil carrying current has radius ' $R$ '. The distance from the centre of the coil on the axis where the magnetic induction will be $\frac{1}{27}$ th to its value at the centre of the coil is
67673.sol:
The magnetic induction B at distance $x$ along the axis of a circular coil of radius $R$ carrying current $I$ is given by $B_x = \frac{\mu_0 I R^2}{2(R^2 + x^2)^{3/2}}$.

At the coil’s center ($x = 0$), the magnetic field simplifies to $B_c = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2R}$.

Given $B_x = \frac{1}{27} B_c$, substitute the expressions:
$\frac{\mu_0 I R^2}{2(R^2 + x^2)^{3/2}} = \frac{1}{27} \cdot \frac{\mu_0 I}{2R}$.

Cancel the common factors $\mu_0 I / 2$ from both sides:
$\frac{R^2}{(R^2 + x^2)^{3/2}} = \frac{1}{27R}$.

Cross-multiplying yields $27R^3 = (R^2 + x^2)^{3/2}$.
Raising both sides to the power $\frac{2}{3}$ gives $(27R^3)^{2/3} = (R^2 + x^2)$.

Evaluate the left-hand side:
$(3^3 R^3)^{2/3} = 3^2 R^2 = 9R^2$, so $9R^2 = R^2 + x^2$.

Solving for $x^2$: $x^2 = 8R^2$, hence $x = \sqrt{8R^2} = 2\sqrt{2} R$.

The magnetic induction is $\frac{1}{27}$ its central value at a distance $x = 2\sqrt{2} R$ along the axis.

68011.text: Calculate the values of $a$ and $b$ if vectors $a\hat{i} + b\hat{j} = \hat{n}$ and $(\hat{i} + \hat{j})$ are perpendicular to each other
68011.sol:
Given $\vec{v}_1 = a\hat{i} + b\hat{j} = \hat{n}$ and $\vec{v}_2 = \hat{i} + \hat{j}$.

Since $\vec{v}_1$ is a unit vector, its magnitude is $1$.

$a^2 + b^2 = 1$

Since $\vec{v}_1$ and $\vec{v}_2$ are perpendicular, their dot product is zero.

$(a\hat{i} + b\hat{j}) \cdot (\hat{i} + \hat{j}) = 0$

$a + b = 0 \Rightarrow b = -a$

Substituting $b = -a$ in the magnitude equation:

$a^2 + (-a)^2 = 1$

$2a^2 = 1 \Rightarrow a = \pm \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

For $a = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$, $b = -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$.

Answer: $\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right), \left(-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)$

69465.text: I-V characteristics of LED is shown correctly by graph
69465.sol:
The current-voltage characteristics of an LED correspond to those of a p-n junction diode, operating primarily under forward bias where it emits light. Graph (a) represents the full characteristic curve with both forward and reverse bias regions.

In forward bias ($V > 0$, $I > 0$), a small current flows until the knee voltage is exceeded, after which current grows exponentially. In reverse bias ($V < 0$, $I < 0$), only a minimal reverse saturation current flows until breakdown. Graphs (b) and (d) are incomplete or inaccurate as they omit the reverse region or misrepresent the exponential forward behavior, while graph (c) shows invalid operation in the fourth quadrant.

Thus, the correct representation is graph (a).

69479.subject: Physics
69479.text: Which of the following logic gates is called as Universal gate?
69479.sol:
A universal gate implements any Boolean function using only that gate type. The NAND gate and NOR gate are the two universal gates, while OR, XOR, and AND gates are not universal.

Any logic gate can be constructed using only NAND gates: NOT is formed by connecting both NAND inputs together, AND by inverting a NAND output with another NAND, and OR through De Morgan's theorem $A + B = (A' \cdot B')'$ with three NAND gates.

The correct answer is $\boxed{\text{D}}$.

69481.text: In an n-p-n transistor amplifier, the collector current is 8 mA. If $80 \%$ of the electrons from the emitter reach the collector, then (\alpha$ and \beta$ are current ratios)
69481.sol:
Given the collector current $I_C = 8\text{ mA}$ and that $80\%$ of emitter electrons reach the collector, it follows $I_C = 0.80\, I_E$.

$I_E = \frac{8\text{ mA}}{0.80} = 10\text{ mA}$

The emitter current is the sum of the base and collector currents, $I_E = I_B + I_C$, leading to:

$I_B = 10\text{ mA} - 8\text{ mA} = 2\text{ mA}$

The common base current gain is $\alpha = \frac{I_C}{I_E} = \frac{8\text{ mA}}{10\text{ mA}} = 0.8$.

The common emitter current gain is $\beta = \frac{I_C}{I_B} = \frac{8\text{ mA}}{2\text{ mA}} = 4.0$ or equivalently $\beta = \frac{\alpha}{1-\alpha} = \frac{0.8}{0.2} = 4.0$.

This corresponds to option C.

71967.subject: Chemistry
71967.text: Identify from the following pair of solutions on mixing exhibits positive deviation from Raoult's law.
71967.sol:
Chloroform and acetone form intermolecular hydrogen bonds upon mixing, leading to stronger interactions and a negative deviation from Raoult's law.

Carbon disulfide and acetone mixture exhibits a positive deviation because the non-polar carbon disulfide molecules disrupt the strong dipole-dipole interactions between acetone molecules, making the solute-solvent interactions weaker than the solute-solute and solvent-solvent interactions.

Phenol and aniline form strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds, resulting in a negative deviation.

Benzene and toluene form an ideal solution as their intermolecular interactions are similar in magnitude.

Therefore, the mixture of carbon disulfide and acetone exhibits a positive deviation from Raoult's law.

Answer: Carbon disulfide and acetone

72284.subject: Physics
72284.text: $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$ are expressed as $\vec{A}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}$ and $\vec{B}=\hat{i}-\hat{j}$. Unit vector perpendicular to $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$ is
72284.sol:
Given vectors are $\vec{A} = 2\hat{i} + \hat{j}$ and $\vec{B} = \hat{i} - \hat{j}$.

A vector perpendicular to both $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$ is given by their cross product $\vec{A} \times \vec{B}$.

$\vec{A} \times \vec{B} = (2\hat{i} + \hat{j}) \times (\hat{i} - \hat{j})$

$\vec{A} \times \vec{B} = 2(\hat{i} \times \hat{i}) - 2(\hat{i} \times \hat{j}) + (\hat{j} \times \hat{i}) - (\hat{j} \times \hat{j})$

Since $\hat{i} \times \hat{i} = 0$, $\hat{j} \times \hat{j} = 0$, $\hat{i} \times \hat{j} = \hat{k}$, and $\hat{j} \times \hat{i} = -\hat{k}$:

$\vec{A} \times \vec{B} = 0 - 2\hat{k} - \hat{k} - 0 = -3\hat{k}$

The magnitude of this vector is $|\vec{A} \times \vec{B}| = |-3\hat{k}| = 3$.

The unit vector perpendicular to both $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$ is:

$\hat{n} = \dfrac{\vec{A} \times \vec{B}}{|\vec{A} \times \vec{B}|} = \dfrac{-3\hat{k}}{3} = -\hat{k}$

Answer: $-\hat{k}$

73818.text: Which one of the following statements is correct?
options: A neutron is formed by combination of an electron and a proton. Therefore, it is neutral
The mass of an electron is about 1/2000 times that of a proton
An isotope of cobalt is used in the treatment of goiter
J. J. Thomson proposed that the nucleus of an atom contains only neutrons
73818.sol:
Statement 1 is incorrect because a neutron is a fundamental subatomic particle, not a combination of an electron and a proton.

Statement 2 is correct because the mass of an electron is approximately $\dfrac{1}{1837}$ times the mass of a proton, which is roughly $\dfrac{1}{2000}$.

Statement 3 is incorrect because an isotope of iodine (I-131) is used in the treatment of goiter, whereas an isotope of cobalt (Co-60) is used in the treatment of cancer.

Statement 4 is incorrect because J. J. Thomson proposed the plum pudding model of the atom. The nucleus was discovered by Rutherford, and neutrons were discovered by James Chadwick.

Answer: The mass of an electron is about 1/2000 times that of a proton

78018.subject: Mathematics
78018.text:
Passage: Let $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$ be mutually exclusive and exhaustive events and $\dfrac{P(A)}{2}=\dfrac{P(B)}{3}=\dfrac{P(C)}{5}=\dfrac{P(D)}{8}$.

Question: What is $P(A)+P(B)+P(C)$ equal to ?
78018.sol:
Let $\dfrac{P(A)}{2} = \dfrac{P(B)}{3} = \dfrac{P(C)}{5} = \dfrac{P(D)}{8} = k$

$P(A) = 2k$, $P(B) = 3k$, $P(C) = 5k$, $P(D) = 8k$

Since $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$ are mutually exclusive and exhaustive events, $P(A) + P(B) + P(C) + P(D) = 1$

$2k + 3k + 5k + 8k = 1$

$18k = 1 \Rightarrow k = \dfrac{1}{18}$

$P(A) + P(B) + P(C) = 2k + 3k + 5k = 10k$

$10k = 10 \times \dfrac{1}{18} = \dfrac{5}{9}$

Answer: $\dfrac{5}{9}$

79666.subject: Botany
79666.sol:
A plasmid is a small, often circular DNA molecule found in bacteria and other cells. Plasmids are separate from the bacterial chromosome and replicate independently of it.
Related Theory
Each bacterial cell typically produces many copies of a plasmid, in contrast to making only one copy of its own chromosome. The fact that plasmids are smaller and in greater number than the host chromosome make plasmids easier to isolate in pure form, which is why researchers commonly use them for studying DNA in the laboratory. Plasmids are thus a fundamental tool of recombinant DNA technology.

83933.subject: Zoology
83933.text: The inactive form of Bt toxin is converted to the active form in the insect gut __________.
83933.sol:
Bt toxin is produced by the bacterium Bacillus thuringiensis in an inactive form called protoxin.

When an insect ingests this inactive toxin, it enters the gut where the pH is alkaline.

The alkaline pH of the insect gut solubilizes the protein crystals, converting the inactive protoxin into its active form.

The active toxin then binds to the surface of midgut epithelial cells, creating pores that cause cell swelling and lysis, eventually leading to the death of the insect.

Answer: due to alkaline pH

84469.sol: Human infection (transmission) occurs when a female mosquito inoculates the sporozoites of Plasmodium from its salivary gland into the blood of man. The sporozoites invade the cells of the liver and reproduce through multiple fission or sporulation (asexual reproduction) called pre-erythrocytic, exoerythrocytic, or intrahepatic schizogony or merogony. Each sporozoite produces daughter merozoites. These merozoites are released into the bloodstream through the infected liver cell. Once the merozoites are in the blood, they quickly invade RBCs and become trophozoites.

84698.subject: Zoology
84698.sol:
During cleavage, the zygote divides repeatedly to convert the large cytoplasmic mass into a large number of small blastomeres. It involvescell division without growth in size because cells continue to be retained within the zona pellucida. However, cell size decreases during cleavage.
Related Theory
Holoblastic cleavage is a complete cleavage meaning it completely penetrates the egg. Meroblastic cleavage is incomplete or partial cleavage meaning it does not penetrate the egg completely.

84894.subject: Zoology
84894.text: Which of the following features of genetic code does allow bacteria to produce human insulin by recombinant DNA technology?
84894.sol: Although the code is based on work conducted on the bacterium Escherichia coli it is valid for other organisms. This important characteristic of the genetic code is called its universality. It means that the same sequences of 3 bases encode the same amino acids in all life forms from simple microorganisms to complex, multicelled organisms such as human beings.

85548.subject: Zoology
85548.text: Which one of the following is the true description about an animal concerned?
options:
Earthworm -
The alimentary canal consists of a sequence of pharynx, oesophagus, stomach, gizzard and intestine
Frog - Body divisible into three regions- head, neck and trunk
Rat - Left kidney is slightly higher in position than the right one
Cockroach - 10 pairs of spiracles (2 pairs on thorax and 8 pairs on abdomen)
85548.sol:
The respiratory system of cockroach consists of tracheae, tracheoles and spiracles. The main tracheal trunks open to exterior on body surface through 10 pairs of segmentally arranged spiracles. Two pair of spiracles are thoracic (one between pro and mesothorax and other between meso and meta thorax). Eight pairs of spiracle are abdominal (one pair in each of the first eight abdominal segments).
Alimentary canal of earthworm is complete and functionally regioned into buccal chamber, pharynx, oesophagus, gizzard, stomach and intestine.
Frog's body has two main parts, ie, head and trunk. Absence of neck and tail provide convenience in both hopping and swimming.

86456.subject: Mathematics
86456.sol:
Given $\sin^{-1} x - \sin^{-1}\dfrac{1}{4} = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$

$\Rightarrow \sin^{-1} x = \dfrac{\pi}{3} + \sin^{-1}\dfrac{1}{4}$

Taking sine on both sides:

$x = \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3} + \sin^{-1}\dfrac{1}{4}\right)$

Using the identity $\sin(A + B) = \sin A \cos B + \cos A \sin B$:

$x = \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) \cos\left(\sin^{-1}\dfrac{1}{4}\right) + \cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) \sin\left(\sin^{-1}\dfrac{1}{4}\right)$

We know that $\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ and $\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

Let $\theta = \sin^{-1}\dfrac{1}{4}$, then $\sin \theta = \dfrac{1}{4}$.

Since $\theta \in \left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, $\cos \theta = \sqrt{1 - \sin^2 \theta} = \sqrt{1 - \dfrac{1}{16}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{15}}{4}$.

Substituting these values:

$x = \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{15}}{4}\right) + \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) \left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)$

$x = \dfrac{\sqrt{45}}{8} + \dfrac{1}{8}$

$x = \dfrac{3\sqrt{5} + 1}{8}$

$x = \dfrac{1}{8}(1 + 3\sqrt{5})$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{8}(1 + 3\sqrt{5})$

Let, $- x^{2} = v$
$- 2xdx = dv ⇒ \dfrac{e- x^{2}}{( 2x + y )2} = - ∫ e^{v}vdv$

$⇒ sin ⁡ x + cos ⁡ x = \dfrac{2n + 1}{14}$
$⇒ sin ⁡ \left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) =\dfrac{2n + 1}{14\sqrt{2}}$
$- 1 \le sin ⁡ \left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) \le 1$
$- 1 \le \dfrac{2n + 1}{14\sqrt{2}} ⁡ \le 1$
$\dfrac{- 14\sqrt{2} - 1}{2} ⁡ \le n \le\dfrac{14\sqrt{2} - 1}{2}$
$- 10.4 \le n \le 9.4$
$⇒ n = - 10, - 9, \ldots \ldots , - 1, 0, 1, \ldots . , 9$
Total $20$ values of $n$ and for each value of $n$ their will be two solutions.

Hence, $k = 40 ⇒ \dfrac{k}{5} = 8$

93833.text: The edge of an aluminium cube is $10$ cm long. One face of the cube is firmly fixed to a vertical wall. A mass of $100$ kg is then attached to the opposite face of the cube. The shear modulus of aluminium is $25$ GPa. What is the vertical deflection of this face?

$3. 92 \times {10}^{- 7}m$
&
93833.sol:
Given, side of a cube (l) = 10 cm & = 0.1 m

Area its each face (A) = l^{2} = (0.1)^{2} = 0.01 m^{2}

Load (m) = 100 kg

Tangential force acting on one face of the cube,

F = mg = 100 × 9.8 = 980 N

$\text{Shear stress acting on this face} = \dfrac{\text{F}}{\text{A}}$

$= \dfrac{\text{980}}{\text{0.01}} {N/m}^{2}$

= 9.8 × 10^{4} N/m^{2}

Shear modulus of aluminium (η)) = 25 GPa

= 25 × 10^{9} N/m^{2}

$\text{Shear modulus} \left(η\right) = \dfrac{\text{Shearing stress}}{\text{Shearing strain}}$

$\text{or shearing strain} \left(\dfrac{\text{\Delta} \text{y}}{\text{L}}\right) = \dfrac{\text{Shearing stress}}{\text{Shear modulus}}$

$\text{or} \text{\Delta} \text{y} = \dfrac{\text{Shearing stress}}{\text{Shear modulus}} \times \text{L}$

$= \dfrac{\text{9.8} \times {10}^{4}}{\text{25} \times {10}^{9}} \times \text{0.1}$

= 0.392 × 10^{-5} m

= 3.92 × 10^{-7} m

100504.subject: Physics
100504.text: A particle is projected from the ground with a speed of $40 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ at an angle of $30^{\circ}$ with the horizontal. What is the magnitude of the change in its velocity between the point of projection and the highest point of its trajectory?
100504.sol:
Let the point of projection be the origin. The initial velocity vector $\vec{u}$ can be resolved into horizontal and vertical components:

$\vec{u} = u \cos \theta \hat{i} + u \sin \theta \hat{j}$

$\vec{u} = 40 \cos 30^{\circ} \hat{i} + 40 \sin 30^{\circ} \hat{j} = 20\sqrt{3} \hat{i} + 20 \hat{j} \text{ m s}^{-1}$

At the highest point of the trajectory, the vertical component of velocity becomes zero, while the horizontal component remains constant.

Velocity at the highest point, $\vec{v} = 20\sqrt{3} \hat{i} \text{ m s}^{-1}$

The change in velocity vector is $\Delta \vec{v} = \vec{v} - \vec{u}$

$\Delta \vec{v} = (20\sqrt{3} \hat{i}) - (20\sqrt{3} \hat{i} + 20 \hat{j}) = -20 \hat{j} \text{ m s}^{-1}$

The magnitude of the change in velocity is $|\Delta \vec{v}| = 20 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

Answer: $20 \text{ m s}^{-1}$

101412.subject: Physics
101412.text: The work done to raise a body of mass $m$ from the surface of the Earth to a certain height $h$ is $\dfrac{3}{4}mgR$, where $R$ is the radius of the Earth and $g$ is the acceleration due to gravity at the surface. The height $h$ is:
101412.sol:
The change in gravitational potential energy when a mass $m$ is raised to a height $h$ from the Earth's surface is given by:

$W = \Delta U = \dfrac{mgh}{1 + \dfrac{h}{R}}$

Given that the work done is $W = \dfrac{3}{4}mgR$, we can equate the two expressions:

$\dfrac{3}{4}mgR = \dfrac{mgh}{1 + \dfrac{h}{R}}$

Cancelling $mg$ from both sides:

$\dfrac{3}{4}R = \dfrac{h}{1 + \dfrac{h}{R}}$

$\dfrac{3}{4}R = \dfrac{hR}{R + h}$

Cross-multiplying gives:

$3(R + h) = 4h$

$3R + 3h = 4h$

$h = 3R$

Using the incorrect approximation $W = mgh$ would lead to the wrong answer $h = \dfrac{3}{4}R$.

Answer: $3R$

101685.subject: Physics
101685.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): As an air bubble rises from the bottom of a deep lake to the surface, the excess pressure of the air inside it relative to the surrounding water decreases.

Reason (R): The excess pressure inside an air bubble is directly proportional to the radius of the bubble.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
101685.sol:
Assertion (A) is correct: As an air bubble rises, the depth of the water column above it decreases, which reduces the external hydrostatic pressure. According to Boyle's law, as the external pressure decreases, the volume of the air bubble increases, meaning its radius $R$ increases.

The excess pressure inside an air bubble in a liquid is given by $\Delta P = \dfrac{2T}{R}$. Since the radius $R$ increases as the bubble rises, the excess pressure $\Delta P$ must decrease.

Reason (R) is incorrect: The formula $\Delta P = \dfrac{2T}{R}$ shows that the excess pressure is inversely proportional to the radius of the bubble, not directly proportional.

Therefore, (A) is correct but (R) is not correct.

Answer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct

101883.subject: Physics
101883.text: The steady-state temperature ($T$) along a composite rod made of two materials in series is plotted against the distance ($x$) from the hot end. The graph shows a piecewise linear drop such that at $x = 0$, $T = 100^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$; at the junction $x = L$, $T = 80^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$; and at the cold end $x = 3L$, $T = 20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$. Assuming both materials have the same uniform cross-sectional area, what is the ratio of the thermal conductivity of the first material to that of the second material ($K_1 : K_2$)?
101883.sol:
In steady state, the rate of heat flow (heat current) is constant throughout the composite rod.

Let $H_1$ and $H_2$ be the heat currents in the first and second materials respectively.

For the first material (from $x = 0$ to $x = L$):
Temperature difference $\Delta T_1 = 100^{\circ}\mathrm{C} - 80^{\circ}\mathrm{C} = 20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$
Length $L_1 = L$
Heat current $H_1 = \dfrac{K_1 A (20)}{L}$

For the second material (from $x = L$ to $x = 3L$):
Temperature difference $\Delta T_2 = 80^{\circ}\mathrm{C} - 20^{\circ}\mathrm{C} = 60^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$
Length $L_2 = 3L - L = 2L$
Heat current $H_2 = \dfrac{K_2 A (60)}{2L} = \dfrac{K_2 A (30)}{L}$

Since the rods are in series, $H_1 = H_2$:
$\dfrac{K_1 A (20)}{L} = \dfrac{K_2 A (30)}{L}$

$\Rightarrow 20 K_1 = 30 K_2$

$\Rightarrow \dfrac{K_1}{K_2} = \dfrac{30}{20} = \dfrac{3}{2}$

Thus, the ratio $K_1 : K_2$ is $3 : 2$.

Answer: $3 : 2$

106457.text:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the radius of Bohr orbits ($a_0$ is the radius of the first Bohr orbit of a hydrogen atom).

List-I (Orbit and Species)List-II (Radius)
A. $2^{\text{nd}}$ orbit of $\text{Li}^{2+}$I. $4.5 a_0$
B. $3^{\text{rd}}$ orbit of $\text{He}^{+}$II. $2 a_0$
C. $4^{\text{th}}$ orbit of $\text{Be}^{3+}$III. $\dfrac{4}{3} a_0$
D. $2^{\text{nd}}$ orbit of $\text{He}^{+}$IV. $4 a_0$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
106457.sol:
The radius of the $n^{\text{th}}$ Bohr orbit is given by $r_n = a_0 \dfrac{n^2}{Z}$.

A. For $2^{\text{nd}}$ orbit of $\text{Li}^{2+}$ ($n=2, Z=3$):
$r = a_0 \dfrac{2^2}{3} = \dfrac{4}{3} a_0$

B. For $3^{\text{rd}}$ orbit of $\text{He}^{+}$ ($n=3, Z=2$):
$r = a_0 \dfrac{3^2}{2} = 4.5 a_0$

C. For $4^{\text{th}}$ orbit of $\text{Be}^{3+}$ ($n=4, Z=4$):
$r = a_0 \dfrac{4^2}{4} = 4 a_0$

D. For $2^{\text{nd}}$ orbit of $\text{He}^{+}$ ($n=2, Z=2$):
$r = a_0 \dfrac{2^2}{2} = 2 a_0$

Therefore, the correct match is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

Answer: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

\(\Delta S_{\text{Total }}=\Delta S_{\text{System }}+\Delta S_{\text{Surroundings }}\)
We know:
\(\Delta S_{\text{Surroundings }}=-\frac{\Delta H_{\text{System }}}{T}=-\frac{4000}{800}=-\)
So,
\(-80=\Delta S_{\text{System }}-5 \Rightarrow \Delta S_{\text{System }}=-i\)
Therefore, this statement is also incorrect.
Therefore, this statement is also incorrect.
(c) Reaction is non-spontaneous: Since \(\Delta G>0\), this statement is correct.
- (d) Reaction is spontaneous: Since \(\Delta G>0\), this statement is incorrect.

(2) (a), (b), (c).

112658.text: Benzene reacts with propene in the presence of $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ to form compound A. Oxidation of A by $\text{O}_2$ followed by acidic hydrolysis yields an aromatic compound B and an aliphatic compound C. When compound C is treated with $\text{I}_2$ and $\text{NaOH}$, what is the identity of C and the visible observation in this final step?
options: C is propanal; a silver mirror is formed
C is acetic acid; brisk effervescence occurs
C is acetone; a yellow precipitate is formed

112658.sol:
The reaction of benzene with propene in the presence of an acid catalyst ($\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$) is an alkylation reaction that yields cumene (isopropylbenzene) as compound A.

Cumene (A) undergoes air oxidation to form cumene hydroperoxide, which on subsequent acidic hydrolysis yields phenol (aromatic compound B) and acetone (aliphatic compound C, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$).

Acetone (C) contains a methyl ketone group ($\text{-COCH}_3$) and therefore gives a positive iodoform test. When treated with $\text{I}_2$ and $\text{NaOH}$, it undergoes the haloform reaction to produce a yellow precipitate of iodoform ($\text{CHI}_3$) and sodium acetate.

Thus, compound C is acetone and a yellow precipitate is formed.

Answer: C is acetone; a yellow precipitate is formed

113898.subject: Chemistry
113898.text: A gas cylinder contains a binary mixture of argon and krypton. If the partial pressure of argon is $2.4\text{ atm}$ and the mole fraction of krypton in the mixture is $0.40$, what is the total pressure of the gas mixture?
113898.sol:
For a binary mixture, the sum of mole fractions is $1$.

Mole fraction of argon ($\chi_{\text{Ar}}$) $= 1 - \text{Mole fraction of krypton}$
$\chi_{\text{Ar}} = 1 - 0.40 = 0.60$

According to Dalton's law of partial pressures:
Partial pressure of argon ($p_{\text{Ar}}$) $= \text{Total pressure} \times \chi_{\text{Ar}}$

Rearranging for total pressure:
$\text{Total pressure} = \dfrac{p_{\text{Ar}}}{\chi_{\text{Ar}}}$
$\text{Total pressure} = \dfrac{2.4\text{ atm}}{0.60} = 4.0\text{ atm}$

Answer: $4.0\text{ atm}$

113903.subject: Chemistry
113903.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): For an ideal solution formed by mixing two volatile liquids, $\Delta_{\text{mix}}H = 0$ and $\Delta_{\text{mix}}V = 0$.
Reason (R): The entropy of mixing ($\Delta_{\text{mix}}S$) for an ideal solution is zero because there is no change in the magnitude of intermolecular forces.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion
Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect
Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct
113903.sol:
Assertion (A) is correct: By definition, when two liquids mix to form an ideal solution, there is no change in enthalpy ($\Delta_{\text{mix}}H = 0$) and no change in volume ($\Delta_{\text{mix}}V = 0$).

Reason (R) is incorrect: The entropy of mixing ($\Delta_{\text{mix}}S$) is always positive ($\Delta_{\text{mix}}S > 0$) for the formation of any solution (ideal or non-ideal). This is because the mixing of two distinct substances increases the randomness or disorder of the system. The absence of change in intermolecular forces does not mean the entropy change is zero.

Therefore, Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.

Answer: Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect

114913.subject: Chemistry
114913.text:
The kinetic data for a chemical reaction is given in the following table:

Time (min)$0$$10$$20$
Concentration ($\mathrm{M}$)$0.40$$0.20$$0.10$


Based on the above data, what will be the concentration of the reactant at $40$ minutes?
114913.sol:
From the table, the concentration of the reactant reduces to half its initial value every $10$ minutes ($0.40 \mathrm{M} \rightarrow 0.20 \mathrm{M} \rightarrow 0.10 \mathrm{M}$).

This constant half-life indicates a first-order reaction with $t_{1/2} = 10 \text{ min}$.

We need to find the concentration at $t = 40 \text{ min}$.

Number of half-lives, $n = \dfrac{t}{t_{1/2}} = \dfrac{40}{10} = 4$

Concentration after $4$ half-lives $= \dfrac{[\mathrm{A}]_0}{2^n} = \dfrac{0.40}{2^4} = \dfrac{0.40}{16} = 0.025 \mathrm{M}$.

Answer: $0.025 \mathrm{M}$

117799.subject: Chemistry
117799.text:
Match List-I with List-II for the corresponding crystal field splitting energies of complexes having the same metal ion, same oxidation state and same ligands.

List-IList-II
(A) $\Delta_o = 36000 \mathrm{cm}^{-1}$(I) $\Delta_o = 18000 \mathrm{cm}^{-1}$
(B) $\Delta_t = 8000 \mathrm{cm}^{-1}$(II) $\Delta_o = 27000 \mathrm{cm}^{-1}$
(C) $\Delta_o = 27000 \mathrm{cm}^{-1}$(III) $\Delta_t = 16000 \mathrm{cm}^{-1}$
(D) $\Delta_t = 12000 \mathrm{cm}^{-1}$(IV) $\Delta_t = 12000 \mathrm{cm}^{-1}$


Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
117799.sol:
The relationship between the crystal field splitting energy of octahedral ($\Delta_o$) and tetrahedral ($\Delta_t$) complexes for the same metal, same oxidation state and same ligands is given by:
$\Delta_t = \dfrac{4}{9} \Delta_o$

Let us calculate the corresponding values for each case in List-I:

(A) Given $\Delta_o = 36000 \mathrm{cm}^{-1}$
$\Delta_t = \dfrac{4}{9} \times 36000 = 16000 \mathrm{cm}^{-1}$. This matches with (III).

(B) Given $\Delta_t = 8000 \mathrm{cm}^{-1}$
$\Delta_o = \dfrac{9}{4} \times \Delta_t = \dfrac{9}{4} \times 8000 = 18000 \mathrm{cm}^{-1}$. This matches with (I).

(C) Given $\Delta_o = 27000 \mathrm{cm}^{-1}$
$\Delta_t = \dfrac{4}{9} \times 27000 = 12000 \mathrm{cm}^{-1}$. This matches with (IV).

(D) Given $\Delta_t = 12000 \mathrm{cm}^{-1}$
$\Delta_o = \dfrac{9}{4} \times 12000 = 27000 \mathrm{cm}^{-1}$. This matches with (II).

Therefore, the correct matching sequence is (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II)

118255.text:
Identify the major product formed when 1-chloro-2-methylpropane is subjected to the following sequence of reactions:

118255.sol:
1-chloro-2-methylpropane reacts with KCN to undergo nucleophilic substitution, forming 3-methylbutanenitrile (an additional carbon is introduced to the main chain).

Acidic hydrolysis of the nitrile group yields 3-methylbutanoic acid.

Finally, treatment with $\text{Br}_2$ and red phosphorus followed by hydrolysis is the Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (HVZ) reaction. This reaction selectively halogenates the $\alpha$-carbon (the carbon adjacent to the carboxyl group).

The $\alpha$-carbon in 3-methylbutanoic acid is a $\text{-CH}_2\text{-}$ group. Replacing one hydrogen with bromine gives 2-bromo-3-methylbutanoic acid.

Answer: 2-bromo-3-methylbutanoic acid

119879.text:
Match List I with List II.

List IList II
(A) Propan-2-amine(I) Hinsberg's reagent
(B) N-methylethanamine(II) Forms an alkali-insoluble solid with Hinsberg's reagent

119879.sol:
(A) Propan-2-amine ($CH_3CH(NH_2)CH_3$) is a primary ($1^{\circ}$) amine. It reacts with Hinsberg's reagent to form a sulphonamide containing an acidic hydrogen, which dissolves in alkali. Hence, (A) matches with (IV).

(B) N-methylethanamine ($CH_3NHCH_2CH_3$) is a secondary ($2^{\circ}$) amine. It reacts with Hinsberg's reagent to form a sulphonamide that lacks an acidic hydrogen, making it insoluble in alkali. Hence, (B) matches with (II).

(C) N,N-dimethylmethanamine ($(CH_3)_3N$) is a tertiary ($3^{\circ}$) amine. It does not react with Hinsberg's reagent to form a stable sulphonamide. Hence, (C) matches with (III).

(D) Benzenesulphonyl chloride ($C_6H_5SO_2Cl$) is known as Hinsberg's reagent. Hence, (D) matches with (I).

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(IV), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(I).

Answer: (A)-(IV), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(I)

122079.subject: Botany
122079.text: Why is vivipary an undesirable character for annual crop plants?
options: it reduces the vigour of the plant
it adversely affects the fertility of the plant
the seeds cannot be stored under normal conditions for the next season.
122079.sol:
Annual plants complete their life cycle in one season, wherein seeds are produced, germinated and the mature plant hence produced, dies within the same season. In vivipary, seeds or spores germinate in situ on mature plants even before they are released which is not possible for annual plants as in them, the mature plants fail to store seeds. This is a result of it dying after seedproduction.
Related Theory
Seeds are structures that contain a young plant inside a protective coating. One reason why seed plants are so numerous is that they produce seeds. Seed plants do not need water in their environment to reproduce like seedless plants do. Even though different kinds of seeds look different from each other, they all have a similar structure. A seed has three important parts: an embryo, stored food, and a seed coat. All seed plants share two characteristics. They have vascular tissue and use seeds to reproduce. In addition, they all have body plans that include leaves, stems, and roots. Most seed plants live on land.

123415.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In a dicotyledonous stem, the innermost layer of the cortex is often referred to as the starch sheath.
Reason (R): The cells of the endodermis in a dicotyledonous stem contain abundant starch grains.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
123415.sol:
In a dicotyledonous stem, the cortex consists of three sub-zones: the outer hypodermis, the middle cortical layers, and the innermost layer called the endodermis.

The cells of the endodermis are rich in starch grains, and because of this characteristic feature, the layer is also referred to as the starch sheath.

Thus, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) correctly explains why the innermost layer of the cortex is called the starch sheath.

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

124274.text:

Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.

124274.sol:
Assertion (A) is true because chromoplasts contain fat-soluble carotenoid pigments like carotene, xanthophylls, and others, which impart yellow, orange, or red colours to plant parts.

Reason (R) is also true because chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and carotenoid pigments that are primarily responsible for trapping light energy essential for photosynthesis.

However, Reason (R) does not explain Assertion (A), as the two statements describe the independent functions and compositions of two different types of plastids.

Therefore, both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.

Answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.

125364.subject: Botany
125364.text: What is another name for the light harvesting system in photosystems?
125364.sol: The pigments are organised into two discrete photochemical light harvesting complexes (LHC) within the Photosystem I (PS I) and Photosystem II (PS II). These are named in the sequence of their discovery, and not in the sequence in which they function during the light reaction. The LHC are made up of hundreds of pigment molecules bound to proteins. Each photosystem has all the pigments (except one molecule of chlorophyll a) forming a light harvesting system also called antennae. These pigments help to make photosynthesis more efficient by absorbing different wavelengths of light. The single chlorophyll a molecule forms the reaction centre. The reaction centre is different in both the photosystems. In PS I the reaction centre chlorophyll a has an absorption peak at 700 nm, hence is called P700, while in PS II it has absorption maxima at 680 nm, and is called P680.

127131.text: How many species on Earth are yet to be discovered and described?
127131.sol: Since there are published records of all the species discovered and named, we know how many species in all have been recorded so far, but it is not easy to answer the question of how many species there are on earth. 127216.text: What is the ethical argument for conserving biodiversity?
127216.sol: The ethical argument for conserving biodiversity relates to what we owe to millions of plant, animal and microbe species with whom we share this planet. Philosophically or spiritually, we need to realise that every species has an intrinsic value, even if it may not be of current or any economic value to us. We have a moral duty to care for their well-being and pass on our biological legacy in good order to future generations.

Have you ever touched the skin of frog? The skin is smooth and slippery due to the presence of mucus. The skin is always maintained in a moist condition. The colour of dorsal side of body is generally olive green with dark irregular spots. On the ventral side the skin is uniformly pale yellow. The frog never drinks water but absorb it through the skin. Body of a frog is divisible into head and trunk A neck and tail are absent. Above the mouth, a pair of nostrils is present. Eyes are bulged and covered by a nictitating membrane that protects them while in water. On either side of eyes a membranous tympanum (ear) receives sound signals. The forelimbs and hind limbs help in swimming, walking, leaping and burrowing. The hind limbs end in five digits and they are larger and muscular than fore limbs that end in four digits. Feet have webbed digits that help in swimming. Frogs exhibit sexual dimorphism. Male frogs can be distinguished by the presence of sound producing vocal sacs and also a copulatory pad on the first digit of the fore limbs which are absent in female frogs.

128116.subject: Zoology
128116.text:
While observing the epithelial lining of the alimentary canal, a student notes the presence of isolated secretory cells interspersed among the regular epithelial cells.

Identify these cells and their correct glandular classification.
options: Salivary glands, which act as multicellular exocrine glands
Goblet cells, which act as unicellular endocrine glands
Goblet cells, which act as multicellular exocrine glands
Goblet cells, which act as unicellular exocrine glands
128116.sol:
According to NCERT, some of the columnar or cuboidal cells get specialised for secretion and are called glandular epithelium. They are mainly of two types: unicellular, consisting of isolated glandular cells (e.g., goblet cells of the alimentary canal), and multicellular, consisting of clusters of cells (e.g., salivary glands).

Goblet cells secrete mucus, which is released through ducts or tubes, making them exocrine glands. Endocrine glands, on the other hand, are ductless and secrete hormones.

Therefore, the isolated secretory cells in the alimentary canal are goblet cells, and they function as unicellular exocrine glands.

Answer: Goblet cells, which act as unicellular exocrine glands

128595.subject: Zoology
128595.text: A specific hormone acts mainly at the renal tubules and stimulates the reabsorption of $\text{Na}^{+}$ and water, while simultaneously promoting the excretion of $\text{K}^{+}$ and phosphate ions. Identify this hormone along with its specific anatomical source.
options: Aldosterone secreted by the adrenal cortex
Anti-diuretic hormone (ADH) secreted by the posterior pituitary
Aldosterone secreted by the adrenal medulla
Cortisol secreted by the adrenal cortex
128595.sol:
Aldosterone is the main mineralocorticoid in the human body. It acts mainly at the renal tubules and stimulates the reabsorption of $\text{Na}^{+}$ and water, and the excretion of $\text{K}^{+}$ and phosphate ions.

Aldosterone is secreted by the adrenal cortex.

Anti-diuretic hormone (ADH) from the posterior pituitary facilitates water reabsorption from the latter parts of the tubule but does not primarily drive $\text{Na}^{+}$/$\text{K}^{+}$ exchange.

Cortisol is a glucocorticoid from the adrenal cortex that produces anti-inflammatory reactions and regulates carbohydrate metabolism.

The adrenal medulla secretes catecholamines (adrenaline and noradrenaline), not aldosterone.

Answer: Aldosterone secreted by the adrenal cortex

129483.subject: Zoology
129483.text: What is the innermost part of the kidney?
129483.sol: In humans, the excretory system consists of a pair of kidneys, one pair of ureters, a urinary bladder and a urethra (Figure 16.1). Kidneys are reddish brown, bean shaped structures situated between the levels of last thoracic and third lumbar vertebra close to the dorsal inner wall of the abdominal cavity. Each kidney of an adult human measures 10-12 cm in length, 5-7 cm in width, 2-3 cm in thickness with an average weight of 120- 170 g. Towards the centre of the inner concave surface of the kidney is a notch called hilum through which ureter, blood vessels and nerves enter. Inner to the hilum is a broad funnel shaped space called the renal pelvis with projections called calyces. The outer layer of kidney is a tough capsule. Inside the kidney, there are two zones, an outer cortex and an inner medulla. The medulla is divided into a few conical masses (medullary pyramids) projecting into the calyces (sing.: calyx). The cortex extends in between the medullary pyramids as renal column called Columns of Bertini (Figure 16.2).

131549.subject: Zoology
131549.text: How does insertion or deletion of three or its multiple bases affect the reading frame in DNA?
options: It changes the reading frame from the point of insertion or deletion
It changes one or multiple amino acids
It has no effect on the reading frame
131549.sol: A classical example of point mutation is a change of single base pair in the gene for beta globin chain that results in the change of amino acid residue glutamate to valine. It results in a diseased condition called sickle cell anemia. Effect of point mutations that inserts or deletes a base in structural genes can be better understood by following simple examples. Insertion or deletion of one or two bases changes the reading frame from the point of insertion or deletion. However, such mutations are referred to as frameshift insertion or deletion mutations. Insertion or deletion of three or its multiple bases insert or delete in one or multiple codons hence one or multiple amino acids, and the reading frame remains unaltered from that point onwards.

They were the first to elucidate a transcriptionally regulated system. In lac operon (here lac refers to lactose), a polycistronic structural gene is regulated by a common promoter and regulatory genes. Such arrangement is very common in bacteria and is referred to as operon. To name a few such examples, lac operon, trp operon, ara operon, his operon, val operon, etc.

132231.subject: Zoology
132231.text: What is the haploid diploid sex-determination system?
options: A system where males have more chromosomes than females
A system where both sexes have the same number of chromosomes
A system where males are haploid and females are diploid
A system where males and females have different sex chromosomes
132231.sol: The sex determination in honey is based on the number of sets of chromosomes an individual receives. An offspring formed from the union of a sperm and an egg develops as a female (queen or worker), and an unfertilised egg develops as a male (drone) by means of parthenogenesis. This means that the males have half the number of chromosomes than that of a female. The females are diploid having 32 chromosomes and males are haploid, i.e., having 16 chromosomes. This is called sex-determination system and has special characteristic features such as the males produce sperms by mitosis (Figure 4.13), they do not have father and thus cannot have sons, but have a grandfather and can have grandsons.
132231.meta: What is the haploid diploid sex-determination system?

132464.subject: Zoology
132464.text: In a certain insect species, the females possess 32 chromosomes in their somatic cells while the males possess 16 chromosomes. The males develop from unfertilized eggs and produce gametes by mitosis. Which of the following terms correctly identifies this specific mechanism of sex determination?
132464.sol:
The scenario describes a system where females are diploid (32 chromosomes) and males are haploid (16 chromosomes).

Since males develop from unfertilized eggs, they are haploid and must produce gametes by mitosis to maintain the chromosome number.

This mechanism, where sex is determined by the number of sets of chromosomes an individual receives, is called the haplodiploid sex-determination system.

The XX-XO type is found in grasshoppers, where males have one less chromosome than females but both are diploid. The ZZ-ZW type is found in birds, where females are heterogametic. Environmental sex determination relies on external factors like temperature, not ploidy differences.

Answer: Haplodiploid sex-determination system

133150.text: What are the consequences of drug and alcohol abuse on health?
133150.sol: Good health can be maintained through a balanced diet, personal hygiene, regular exercise, awareness about diseases, proper disposal of waste, control of vectors, and hygienic food and water resources. Diseases can be broadly categorized into infectious and non-infectious diseases. Infectious diseases are easily transmitted from person to person, while non-infectious diseases include cancer and other health conditions.Drug and alcohol abuse adversely affects health, not increases longevity or productivity.A person is considered not healthy when the functioning of one or more organs or systems of the body is adversely affected by various signs and symptoms, also known as having a disease, not just physical fitness, balanced diet and regular exercise, or good mental health.

133157.sol: In severe cases, typhoid fever can lead to intestinal perforation and death. Mary Mallon was a cook by profession and was a typhoid carrier who continued to spread typhoid for several years through the food she prepared. Salmonella typhi is a pathogenic bacterium which causes typhoid fever in human beings.Salmonella typhi is a pathogenic bacterium which causes typhoid fever in human beings. These pathogens generally enter the small intestine through food and water contaminated with them and migrate to other organs through blood. Sustained high fever (39° to 40°C), weakness, stomach pain, constipation, headache and loss of appetite are some of the common symptoms of this disease. Intestinal perforation and death may occur in severe cases.

133167.subject: Zoology
133167.text: What is the most serious form of malaria caused by Plasmodium?
133167.sol: Malaria is caused by a tiny protozoan named Plasmodium.Malignant malaria, which is the most serious form of malaria, is caused by Plasmodium falciparum. Plasmodium enters the human body as sporozoites (infectious form) through the bite of infected female Anopheles mosquito.The female Anopheles mosquito is the vector (transmitting agent) in the life cycle of Plasmodium. The sporozoites of Plasmodium are stored in the salivary glands of the mosquito and when the mosquito bites a human, the sporozoites are introduced into their body.

133229.subject: Zoology
133229.text: What type of immunity is provided to the newborn infant through mother’s milk?
133229.sol: Active immunity is slow and takes time to give its full effective response when a host is exposed to antigens.Passive immunity is the term used for the process of injecting ready-made antibodies to protect the body against foreign agents.Colostrum is the yellowish fluid secreted by the mother during the initial days of lactation.The primary and secondary immune responses are carried out with the help of two special types of lymphocytes present in our blood, i.e., B-lymphocytes and T-lymphocytes.B-lymphocytes produce an army of proteins in response to pathogens in our blood to fight them. These proteins are called antibodies. Mother’s milk contains abundant antibodies (IgA) and provides passive immunity to the newborn infant.

133756.text: What is the purpose of pumping a part of the activated sludge back into the aeration tank?
options: To release the effluent into natural water bodies
To digest the bacteria in the sludge
133756.sol: Once the BOD of sewage or waste water is reduced significantly, the effluent is then passed into a settling tank where the bacterial ‘flocs’ are allowed to sediment. This sediment is called activated sludge. A small part of the activated sludge is pumped back into the aeration tank to serve as the inoculum. The remaining major part of the sludge is pumped into large tanks called anaerobic sludge digesters.
